subject.title: [Bug]: Code Mode rejects harmless template literals and regular expressions as module access

question: Should Code Mode retain its pre-guest module-access block using a grammar-aware scanner/parser boundary that permits inert literal content while continuing to reject executable module-capability syntax?
rationale: The requested false-positive correction sits directly on the capability-denial boundary; maintainers need to confirm the acceptable implementation approach and the executable forms that must remain fail-closed.

options.title: Approve a bounded grammar-aware repair
options.body: Confirm current-main reproduction and accept a focused validator repair with positive literal/regex cases and negative executable-module cases.

options.title: Keep the current fail-closed scanner
options.body: Retain the existing conservative behavior if the parser/scanner complexity is judged too risky for the Code Mode security boundary.

recommendation.title: Approve a bounded grammar-aware repair
recommendation.body: Confirm current-main reproduction and accept a focused validator repair with positive literal/regex cases and negative executable-module cases.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete supplied the detailed reproduction and explicit safe-versus-executable acceptance criteria that a maintainer decision must evaluate.
